newsitem.title: UK: Nigeria raises most January crude prices.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria raises most January crude prices.

text.p: Nigeria has increased its price formulas for most crude grades loading in January but reduced the price of two, Escravos and Brass River, trade sources said.
Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) told customers the January price of Bonny Light and Qua Iboe would rise five cents from December to Dated Brent plus 50 cents.
Forcados was increased by 10 cents to Dated Brent plus 60 cents.
Bonny Medium also went up 10 cents to Dated Brent plus 50 cents.
Pennington for January was raised five cents to Dated Brent plus 85 cents.
Brass River was reduced by three cents to Dated Brent plus 38 cents and Escravos cut two cents to Dated Brent plus 38 cents.
NNPC raised the premium payable for deferred pricing of January liftings, 14 days after bill of lading, by four cents to 10 cents.
NNPC would continue its new policy of the later release of monthly contract price terms, an NNPC official said.
Prices would be released any time between the 15th of the month prior to loading to the 10th of the month of loading, the official said.
NNPC decided in November to change its pricing procedures because an ever-more opaque market in Nigerian crudes had made it difficult to judge contract prices in the month ahead of lifting.
While spot deals were kept confidential, occasional off-market trades emerged in a bid to influence media price assessments.
The NNPC official said the market in Nigerian crudes appearded to have responded favourably to the policy change.
"It appears customers and traders have responded positively," he said.
Nigeria sells some 850,000 barrels a day of crude through about 30 contracts with traders and refiners, adjusting prices every month according to spot market values.
